newsitem.title: UK: BP, Shell Q2 profit seen higher.
newsitem.headline: BP, Shell Q2 profit seen higher.

text.p: Higher chemical and downstream earnings are seen the main drivers for healthy second quarter profit growth at British Petroleum and Royal Dutch/Shell Group .
Europe's two biggest oil companies release their results next week after the American majors set the tone late last month with bullish profits which beat market forecasts.
Higher profits for Shell Oil from the U.S. and record earnings for Shell Canada bode well for the results of their Anglo-Dutch parent, analysts said.
They predict net income for Shell Group to range between 1.26 billion and 1.48 billion pounds.
Shell, the world's biggest profit maker, posted comparative earnings of 1.187 billion pounds in the same 1996 quarter.
Shell's results are due out on Thursday after British Petroleum (BP) has released its set of figures on Tuesday.
Forecasts for BP vary between 630 million and 690 million pounds compared with 587 million pounds a year earlier.
"Chemicals and downstream have pushed profits higher. It's the same story for Shell," said Fergus Macleod, analyst at broker NatWest Markets.
Estimates for both BP and Shell exclude exceptional items and strip out swings in oil stock values due to commodity price changes.
The price of the main commodity -- crude oil -- fell by about $1.5 per barrel in the second quarter with the benchmark IPE Brent crude down at an average $18.47 from $19.05.
But production growth will have shielded both BP and Shell from the negative price impact, industry watchers said.
Of the two, BP is more geared towards the upstream business and its shares therefore more linked to the oil price than Shell's.
Since prices came under pressure in February, BP has underperformed Shell by some 12 percent, Reuter price data show.

Some analysts said it was time for this trend to be reversed. They predict relatively stable oil prices, but fear lower petrochemicals income next year which would cost Shell "We like BP's upstream exposure and are quite cautious on the chemicals outlook," an analyst said.
Others, however, said they still favoured Shell on valuation grounds even though the gap in cash flow multiples has narrowed substantially recently.
One cautious Shell supporter said he put the cash flow multiple for BP at 9.8, while Shell's multiple had caught up to a current level of 9.7.

-- Hans de Jongh, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 Shell shares outperformed BP's in the wake of depressed oil prices. with some 77 percent of first operating profit stemming from production and exploration activities.
The comparative figure for Shell was 70 percent.
